data.name: Maher
data.gender_notes: Maher is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who gives and heals, a giver, a benefactor. The name Maher carries the meaning “Giver, Healer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Maher usually hope their child will grow to embody giver, healer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A protector, a giver of blessings and healing energy
data.etymology: Maher belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giver, Healer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maher total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Maher" has cultural significance in the Arabic-speaking Muslim world. It is a name that reflects generosity, kindness, and benevolence, which are valued traits in Islamic culture. Maher is a name that is often given to children, emphasizing the importance of giving and helping others from a young age.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Maher" underscores the Islamic belief in the importance of giving and helping others selflessly. In Islamic tradition, it is said that giving to others, especially to those in need, brings spiritual rewards and generates blessings in this life and the next. The name "Maher" serves as a reminder of this fundamental Islamic principle and encourages individuals to cultivate the habit of giving and healing, both materially and emotionally, to those around them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Giver, Healer" symbolizes One who gives and heals, a giver, a benefactor. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Maher serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of giver, healer.
